authoring.protocol: crates/fathom-analyze/calibration/g3/README.md §2 (what each act means) and §3 (how blame is assigned)
authoring.annotated_on: 2026-10-19 (e4.9, 60-episode window), 2026-10-20 (reco-dyt, the same pins re-fetched at a 180-episode window) and 2026-10-20 (reco-6co, the labels the re-scored cut promoted)
authoring.meaning: One row per flagged episode: what the reviewer would have done with the flag, and what they read to decide it. `accepted` means the flag earned the read — the episode was worth stopping for, whatever the findings said. `dismissed` names a code from the closed vocabulary `e4.6` ships, and `blame` names which part of the flag was the false alarm: `score` when the ranking raised a flag no finding justified, a detector id when that detector's claim is what did not hold. A dismissal with no `blame` charges every detector that spoke on the episode, which is ADR-001 §5.4's own rule — an unwanted flag charges whatever raised it.

labels.note: A new 189-line Dependabot triage script and a new scheduled workflow: the flag's claim is that an operator has to act on a workflow change, and a new scheduled job under `permissions:` is exactly that. The two `# shellcheck disable=SC2016` lines `lint_escape` named are inside the script that had to be read anyway, so the finding cost nothing extra.

The commit says they were regenerated — "upgrade gh-aw from v0.87.5 to v0.89.21 and recompile lock files" — so the claim does not describe the change: the detector can tell a generated file from a hand-written one, but not a regeneration from a hand edit. labels.note: All three `test_weakening` claims are the same act: this commit made a font mandatory for rendering, and moved font selection out of the execution contract, so the native-rendering cases now skip with `Supply an explicit font for native rendering.` instead of failing where no font was selected. The cases are still in the file and still run when a font is supplied. Gating a case on a precondition it cannot meet is exactly what was wanted here.

labels.note: Promoted into the flagged set when `reco-6co` stopped charging a bot's compiled workflow lock the CI weight, and it earns the read. The source of an agentic workflow that mints GitHub App tokens moved its pin from an immutable SHA (`create-github-app-token@64ab729a62…`) to a mutable tag (`@v3.3.0`) so the compiler resolves and records the version; what runs today is the same commit, but the source now floats on a tag anyone can move, and `actions-lock.json` gained the entry that decides what it resolves to. That is a provenance decision about a secrets-holding workflow, which is exactly what the workflow axis claims.
labels.evidence: `git show 1ea48c8252`: `.github/workflows/issue-triage.md` line 121 `uses: actions/create-github-app-token@64ab729a62…  # v3.3.0` → `@v3.3.0`; `.github/aw/actions-lock.json` +5 (new `create-github-app-token@v3.3.0` entry, sha `64ab729a62`); `.github/workflows/issue-triage.lock.yml` recompiled (`gh-aw-manifest` records `version: v3.3.0` where it had recorded the SHA).
